title: Add public post-incident summary format + examples (aligned with internal template)
author: Elliot Price
description: This PR introduces a standardized, public-facing post-incident summary format and two example summaries, aligned with the internal Confluence template used by SRE/Comms Leads as part of the Status Page Transparency Upgrades initiative. Motivation: customers have asked for consistent, quickly publishable summaries with clear impact/timeline/prevention detail (ref SUP-28502 and recent status accuracy escalations), and our existing docs do not define what a “post-incident summary” contains or what we will/won’t include for sensitive incidents (Dedicated/Private). Summary of changes: (1) Add a new docs page defining the post-incident summary structure (Impact, Timeline, Root cause class, Mitigation, Prevention/Follow-ups, Where to get help) with explicit confidentiality guidance; (2) Add example summaries that demonstrate appropriate level of detail (no customer identifiers, no capacity specifics, no exploit-level info) and consistent phrasing across incident phases; (3) Update the status page docs index and cross-link from the incident communications guidance so Support can point customers to a stable reference; (4) Add wording notes for Dedicated/Private incidents: what may be published publicly vs when we will publish a “limited summary” and where customer-specific detail will live (support ticket / CSM follow-up). Non-goals: changing the actual status page UI, automating summary generation, or committing to new SLAs/TTFU targets in public docs. Rollout plan: publish docs concurrently with the internal training rollout (PM-620) and keep examples as living references; legal/security reviewed language for safe defaults. Screenshots: N/A (text-only).

notable_snippet: Excerpt added to docs/status/post-incident-summaries.md: “We aim to publish a post-incident summary once service is stable and the initial cause/mitigation is understood. Summaries are written to be useful for engineering teams operating production workloads, without disclosing customer-identifying details, sensitive security information, or capacity/architecture specifics that could increase risk. If an incident affects Dedicated or Private deployments, we may publish a limited public summary and provide additional context directly to affected customers via Support/CS.”
review_conversation: Wei Chen (comment): Suggest tightening the “Root cause” section to “Root cause class” to avoid over-promising certainty in early summaries; also add one sentence explicitly stating that numbers may be approximate initially.
Elliot Price (reply): Good call. Updated headings to “Root cause class” and added a note in Timeline/Impact that metrics may be refined as analysis completes.

Kira Thompson (comment): Dedicated/Private language needs to be clearer: we should not imply per-customer status visibility on the public page. Recommend adding “customer-specific impacts are communicated directly” and remove any mention of “tenant-level components.”
Elliot Price (reply): Agreed. Removed tenant-level phrasing and added “customer-specific impacts are communicated directly via Support/CS channels.”
Dev Patel (comment): Please add a short section “How to reference this summary in a support ticket” + link to status page and incident ID conventions so agents can macro it consistently.
Elliot Price (reply): Added a “Where to get help” line that calls out including request IDs + region + timeframe, and ensured the examples include an incident identifier format agents can copy.

Naomi Feldman (comment): Security note: avoid listing exact WAF rules, exploit details, or vendor advisories until cleared. The examples are fine; just add a single explicit bullet to the “Do not include” list.
Elliot Price (reply): Added bullet under “Do not include” to cover exploit-level details and unreviewed vendor/security advisories.
Michael Grant (comment): Legal: remove ‘we will’ commitments around timing; use ‘we aim’ / ‘when feasible’ and avoid implied SLA language.
Elliot Price (reply): Updated timing language throughout to “aim” and “when feasible,” removed any numeric time commitments, and aligned wording with PM-612 policy.
Paula Mendes (approval): Looks aligned with the internal template and tone guidance; examples are strong. Approved after latest copy edits.
release_notes: Public docs now include a standardized post-incident summary format and examples, aligned with internal incident comms templates; includes guidance on sensitive details and Dedicated/Private handling.
